newsitem.title: CHILE: Accident at El Abra mine traps miners, hits output.
newsitem.headline: Accident at El Abra mine traps miners, hits output.

text.p: An accident on a conveyor belt at Chile's El Abra mine has trapped an unknown number of workers beneath rubble and affected production at the mine, El Abra said.

A brief statement issued by the mine, owned by Cyprus Amax Minerals and state copper firm Codelco, gave no details but said a "serious accident...left an unknown number of workers trapped beneath rubble."
The accident occurred on the conveyor belt stretching from the mine to the heap-leaching plant, said the statement.
Asked if the accident would affect production at the mine, a spokesman said by telephone from the mine, "Indirectly, yes."

The statement did not say if the accident involved a landslide or if the workers were trapped beneath something man-made. It said they were working on a covering that protects the conveyor belt when the accident occurred.
"At this time we can only inform that El Abra and all its subcontractors are carrying out all possible efforts to reach the place where the workers are trapped," it said.
The 11-kilometer conveyor belt carries ore from the open pit mine to the crushers, from where the ore is taken on to heap leaching pads. Much of it passes through a narrow, rocky gorge.
The mine began production in August and is due to climb to 225,000 tonnes of copper a year next year, making it one of Chile's largest mines.
